messages.subject: Re: HTTP authentication
messages.body_plain:
Hi, please have a look to the following login page I did with rApache. It's very basic, but it's a good start to implement a more complex session management. https://github.com/nigmastar/rApacheLogin HTH Michele Carriero On Friday, 28 February 2014 15:41:56 UTC, c0...@arcor.de wrote: > Hello rApache users, > > Is it possible to issue an HTTP authentication request to the user using rApache/Rook and remember the login? > > I want to have a similar behaviour as doing in php: > if (!isset($_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER'])) { > header('WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="My Realm"'); > header('HTTP/1.0 401 Unauthorized'); > echo 'Text to send if user hits Cancel button'; > exit; > } else { > echo "

Hello {$_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER']}.

"; > echo "

You entered {$_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_PW']} as your password.

"; > } > ?> > > The first time a login-form is displayed and the next times, $_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER'] and $_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_PW'] are set accordingly. > When user and password have been provided, I next want to validate MD5 hash of the password by quering an existing database. > > > > Using Rook I have tried the following: > > app <- function(env){ > req <- Request$new(env) > res <- Response$new() > > #res$header('WWW-Authenticate','Basic realm="My Realm"'); res$status <- 401L > res$header('WWW-Authenticate','Basic'); res$status <- 401L > res$write('

Authorization required

\n') > res$write( res$status ) > res$finish() > } > > > However, I am not being asked for the password and the h1 line is displayed immediately. > I tried i both on the R server and on the Apache where the code above is called as described in > http://jeffreyhorner.tumblr.com/post/27861973339/deploy-rook-apps-with-rapache-part-i > > How can I retrieve the values from the Request object, as they are provided in php with $_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_USER'] and $_SERVER['PHP_AUTH_PW']? > > If HTTP authentication is not supported, what is the recommended way to implement access restrictions using rApache/Rook? > > Yours, > Thomas > >

messages.subject: Re: rApache module in Apache error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Please check if /usr/local/lib/R/library is in path. Can you access RApacheInfo? You'll find in there the locations where R looks for installed packages.

Michele Carriero.

On Friday, 28 February 2014 14:17:35 UTC, Daniel Perondi wrote:
> I'm using ubuntu 13.10 with Apache2 , PHP5 and MySQL
> I'm trying to add rApache module in Apache to work as a server R.
>
> I configured my rapache exactly how this turorial shows .
>
> http://binfalse.de/2011/05/r-for-the-web/
>
> One file is created /etc/apache2/mods-available/r.conf
>
> In this file , and put
>
>     <Location /R>
>       ROutputErrors
>       SetHandler r-script
>       RHandler sys.source
>     </Location>
>
>     <Location /RApacheInfo>
>       SetHandler r-info
>     </Location>
>
> I add another "location"
>
>     <Location /brew>
>       SetHandler r-script
>       RHandler brew::brew
>     </Location>
>
> in /brew directory I created a file called plot.R with the code :
>
>     <%
>
>     args <- 'brew work'
>     print(args)
>
>     %>
>
> localhost/brew/plot.R if I try to access the page is loading endlessly and program files /var/log/apache2/error.log displays the error :
>
>      Error in library(brew) : there is no package called 'brew'
>       From directive RHandler on line 3 of /etc/apache2/mods-enabled/r.conf.
>
> I 've tried to install R in the brew package
>
>      install.packages("brew","/usr/local/lib/R/library")
>
> but my error keeps appearing and I can not run the script plot.R
messages.body_snippet:
Hi,

Please check if /usr/local/lib/R/library is in path. Can you access RApacheInfo? You'll find in there the locations where R looks for installed packages.

Michele Carriero.

On Friday, 28 Februar
